source.version: Journal version of record, Frontiers in Psychology 17:1847432, published 17 June 2026; DOI 10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1847432 (p. 1).
source.title_on_document: Effects of integrating a structured design thinking strategy into generative AI-supported design learning on students’ design achievement, creative self-efficacy, and problem-solving skills

supplement.holds: The main text identifies Supplementary Table S1 as the Double Diamond-Based Design Operation Sheet (DDDOS), with stage objectives, self-monitoring questions, suggested GAI use, and stage completion checks (p. 5, section 3.3). It identifies no outcome statistics available only in the supplement. The supplement is outside this PDF and was not inspected; its full contents are unconfirmed.

paper_design_summary: In a university character-design course in China, 120 animation undergraduates were individually randomly assigned to structured design thinking plus generative AI, free use of the same AI tools, or traditional design learning (p. 4, sections 3.1-3.2). Students independently created card-game character artwork, which instructors rated with a design-quality rubric including Creativity; AI remained available during production in the AI arms (pp. 5-9, sections 3.3-3.5; p. 11, section 5.1). The other reported endpoints were questionnaires on creative self-efficacy and perceived problem-solving ability (p. 8, section 3.4).

assignment.what_was_assigned: Three of six existing classes were sampled, then individual students were randomly assigned to GAI-SDTS, GAI, or TDL and reorganized into mixed-class groups (p. 4, section 3.2). The authors call the design quasi-experimental despite explicitly describing individual random assignment.
assignment.quote: All students in the selected classes were then randomly assigned to one of three groups:
assignment.locator: p. 4, sections 3.1-3.2, especially Population and sampling; p. 9, Figure 8. The quasi-experimental label starts on p. 3, section 3.1.

arms.name: GAI-SDTS
arms.description: Deepseek and Dreamina with a Double Diamond-Based Design Operation Sheet guiding Discover, Define, Develop, and Deliver; both AI arms received operational training before the design tasks (pp. 5-8, sections 3.3-3.5). Initial N = 40 in Figure 8 and analyzed N = 40 in Table 1 (p. 9).

arms.name: GAI
arms.description: Free use of the same Deepseek and Dreamina tools without structured design-thinking guidance; the same operational training as GAI-SDTS (p. 5, section 3.3; pp. 8-9, section 3.5). Initial N = 40 in Figure 8 and analyzed N = 40 in Table 1 (p. 9).

arms.name: TDL
arms.description: Traditional Design Learning using printed/online references, hand-drawn sketches, and conventional software such as Photoshop, without GAI or explicit design thinking (pp. 4-5). Initial N = 40 in Figure 8 and analyzed N = 40 in Table 1 (p. 9).

participants.exclusions: No exclusions or attrition are reported. Methods give 120 participants and random assignment of all selected students; Figure 8 shows 40 per condition before pre-questionnaires, and Table 1 analyzes 40 per condition. No separate participant-flow accounting or explicit intention-to-treat claim is provided (p. 4, section 3.2; p. 9, Figure 8 and Table 1).
participants.who: Second-year undergraduate animation majors at one university in central China.
participants.quote: A total of 120 students aged between 19 and 22 years (M = 20.4, SD = 0.84) participated in the experiment.
participants.locator: p. 4, section 3.2, for total participants and assignment; p. 9, Figure 8, for initial arm counts; p. 9, Table 1, for analyzed arm counts.

ai_tool.name_model: Deepseek and Dreamina. Dreamina screenshots show 图片 4.5 (Images 4.5; p. 7, Figure 6, parameter-setting selector) and 图片 4.1 (Images 4.1; p. 8, Figure 7, generated-image information). These are illustrated interface labels; the Methods do not establish which versions participants used throughout the experiment or specify the Deepseek model version (pp. 5-9, sections 3.3-3.5).
ai_tool.how_used: Deepseek supported open text dialogue, ideation, character concepts, prompts, and design statements. Dreamina supported text-to-image and image-to-image generation, variation, refinement, and final export. Structured use in GAI-SDTS and free use in GAI (pp. 5-7, section 3.3). Open chat and refinement were additional roles.

task.description: Independently create a distinctive card-game character with clear personality traits, through exploration, definition, creation, and presentation (p. 4, sections 3.2-3.3). Final artwork was graded (p. 9, section 3.5).
task.duration: Four-week intensive practical course, October 20 to November 14, 2025 (p. 4, section 3.2). The full experimental schedule includes Week 1 pretests and 90 minutes of operational training for both AI arms, design work in Weeks 2-5 at 90 minutes/week, and final-artwork grading and questionnaires in Week 6 (pp. 8-9, section 3.5; p. 9, Figure 8).

outcomes.name: Design achievement: composite expert rating of final character artwork
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Two instructors with 8 years of design teaching experience independently rated anonymized, randomly ordered final artwork. The rubric comprises Technical Skill; Adherence to Theme; Composition and Design; Creativity; and Detail Quality and Workload, each rated from 1 (lowest) to 5 (highest). Kendall’s W = 0.94, p < 0.001 (p. 8, section 3.4). Only the combined design-achievement score is reported; separate dimension results and the aggregation rule across dimensions and raters are not supplied. Coded usefulness under the codebook because it is a broad output-quality composite containing creativity. The analysis compares students’ design-achievement scores, using a one-way ANOVA (p. 9, sections 4-4.1 and Table 1).
outcomes.delay: Course-end grading in Week 6 of final artwork produced during Weeks 2-5 with AI available in the AI arms (p. 9, section 3.5). No new delayed or unassisted production task is described; the scored outputs were generated and refined with AI (p. 11, section 5.1). No delay in days is stated.

contrasts.reported: GAI: M = 18.65, SD = 7.41, N = 40; TDL: M = 16.13, SD = 6.85, N = 40. Tukey HSD: GAI > TDL, p < 0.001. Three-group omnibus ANOVA: F = 43.28, p < 0.001 (not a pairwise test). No standardized effect, contrast standard error, or confidence interval is printed.
contrasts.locator: p. 9, Table 1 and section 4.1, Design achievement results.

contrasts.reported: GAI-SDTS: M = 20.90, SD = 7.64, N = 40; TDL: M = 16.13, SD = 6.85, N = 40. Tukey HSD: GAI-SDTS > TDL, p < 0.001. Three-group omnibus ANOVA: F = 43.28, p < 0.001 (not a pairwise test). No standardized effect, contrast standard error, or confidence interval is printed.
contrasts.locator: p. 9, Table 1 and section 4.1, Design achievement results.

contrasts.reported: GAI-SDTS: M = 20.90, SD = 7.64, N = 40; GAI: M = 18.65, SD = 7.41, N = 40. Tukey HSD: GAI-SDTS > GAI, p < 0.001. Three-group omnibus ANOVA: F = 43.28, p < 0.001 (not a pairwise test). No standardized effect, contrast standard error, or confidence interval is printed.
contrasts.locator: p. 9, Table 1 and section 4.1, Design achievement results.

eligibility.reason: Individual random assignment to two generative-AI conditions or conventional non-AI coursework is explicit; students were reorganized across sampled classes, despite the authors' quasi-experimental label (pp. 3-4, sections 3.1-3.2). Table 1 reports 40 analyzed students in each arm, for 120 analyzed people across the study (p. 4, section 3.2; p. 9, Table 1). Instructors rated students' final character artwork using a rubric explicitly including Creativity alongside other design-quality dimensions (p. 8, section 3.4). AI was available while the scored artwork was produced (pp. 5-9, sections 3.3-3.5; p. 11, section 5.1). All three criteria are met; field_rct reflects the reported random assignment within university coursework. The endpoint is a broad design-quality composite, coded usefulness; a separate creativity-dimension effect is not reported. Unspecified implementation details, the screenshot-version clarification, and unresolved statistical reporting inconsistencies do not change these eligibility findings.

one_line_finding: Among 120 analyzed students, mean design-achievement scores were 20.90 with structured design thinking plus AI, 18.65 with free AI use, and 16.13 with traditional learning; all pairwise p < 0.001 are reported (p. 9, Table 1 and section 4.1).
open_questions: The printed means, SDs, group sizes, omnibus F = 43.28, and all-pairs p < 0.001 appear internally inconsistent; corrected values cannot be established from the PDF. Preserve the printed values and verify against underlying data before extraction (p. 9, Table 1 and section 4.1).
Separate Creativity-dimension results and the aggregation rule across rubric dimensions and the two raters are not supplied (p. 8, section 3.4; p. 9, Table 1).
Individual random assignment is explicit, but sequence generation and implementation are not specified; the authors also use a quasi-experimental label (pp. 3-4, sections 3.1-3.2).

Figure 1 labels design achievement as one-way ANCOVA and questionnaire outcomes as one-way ANOVA, reversing the Results and table titles. Coding follows the explicit Results and Table 1 for design achievement; the reason for the diagram discrepancy is not stated (p. 4, Figure 1; pp. 9-11, Results and Tables 1-3).

Dreamina screenshots show Images 4.5 and Images 4.1, but the Methods do not establish which versions participants used throughout the experiment or specify the Deepseek model version (p. 7, Figure 6; p. 8, Figure 7; pp. 5-9, sections 3.3-3.5).

The external supplement is identified as the Double Diamond-Based Design Operation Sheet in Supplementary Table S1; its complete contents remain uninspected. Requests to the printed Frontiers supplement link and the article DOI both failed with WinError 10013 (p. 5, section 3.3; p. 14, Supplementary material).
notes: Reconciled on 2026-10-09. Both raw forms parsed. The complete markdown conversion was read in consecutive chunks through the final reference; the PDF has no appended supplement. Eligibility facts, recorded numbers, disclosures, and supplement references were checked against PDF text; Table 1 was also recovered with PyMuPDF find_tables, and Figures 1 and 8 were inspected as images in memory. The output inventory contains one design-achievement composite. Creative self-efficacy, creative ideas self-efficacy, creative performance self-efficacy, problem-solving skills, problem-solving confidence, approach-avoidance style, and personal control are self-report questionnaires and are excluded from outcomes (p. 8, section 3.4; pp. 10-11, Tables 2-3). Rubric dimensions have no separately reported results. No across-people diversity or after-AI output is reported. Conventional references and Photoshop comprise usual design learning, so comparisons with TDL are ai_vs_bau; structured AI versus free AI is ai_design. Contrasts share the same sample and comparison arms. No reuse of another paper’s participants is stated; the Bian et al. citation concerns the scoring instrument (p. 8, section 3.4). No public data or code URL is supplied; raw data are promised by the authors (p. 14). The paper does not designate a primary outcome or report preregistration. Reconciliation counts two substantive omissions: minute-level training/task durations supplied only by A, and the Figure 1 analysis-label discrepancy supplied only by B. Additional prose already represented elsewhere in both forms, contrast and open-question ordering, locator wording, and B’s character-encoding errors are not substantive differences. A’s explanatory delay text and B’s blank delay field agree on immediate production with AI; the explanation is retained. Shared source limitations remain in open_questions and do not count as unresolved A-versus-B differences. No effect sizes or replacement statistics were calculated. Finalized on 2026-10-09 after reading all 695 markdown lines through the final references and independently checking the source PDF. The assignment, people, and outcome challenge files contained one problem in total; the Dreamina screenshot-version problem was corrected after enlarged inspection of Figures 6 and 7. Figures 1 and 8 were also inspected, and Table 1 was checked using PDF text and PyMuPDF find_tables. Eligibility remains yes for the reported design and analyzed sample. The existing supplement field meets the current specification; the PDF has no appended supplement or embedded files. Python urllib requests using User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1 to the printed Frontiers supplement URL and DOI both failed with WinError 10013; no external supplement contents were assumed. Every open_questions item is assessed in final.open_items. Both reconciliation differences were already resolved, and the reconciliation object is unchanged. Final challenge counts count checker problems only; the remaining source limitations are tracked separately in final.open_items. Printed statistics are retained without computing replacements or effect sizes.

open_items.item: open_questions[0]: Table 1 means, SDs and group sizes appear inconsistent with the reported omnibus F and all-pairs p values (p. 9, Table 1 and section 4.1). Author-supplied underlying participant scores and analysis output, or corrected statistics, would settle which values are accurate. This affects effect extraction and precision, not the documented assignment, 120 analyzed people, or output scoring.

open_questions[1]: Separate Creativity-dimension results and the rule for aggregating rubric dimensions and the two raters are not supplied (p. 8, section 3.4; p. 9, Table 1). Author clarification of the scoring rule and dimension-level results would settle this. Criterion 3 is already met by expert scoring of final artwork with a rubric that includes Creativity; these details affect interpretation and extraction.

open_questions[2]: Sequence generation and allocation implementation are unspecified alongside the quasi-experimental label (pp. 3-4, sections 3.1-3.2). Author clarification or the allocation protocol would settle the implementation details. Criterion 1 is met by the explicit statement of random assignment of students and their reorganization across sampled classes; the missing details concern assessment of bias.

open_questions[3]: Figure 1 reverses the ANOVA and ANCOVA labels relative to the Results and Tables 1-3 (p. 4, Figure 1; pp. 9-11, sections 4-4.3 and Tables 1-3). An author-confirmed correction or explanation would settle the discrepancy. Design-achievement coding follows the explicit one-way ANOVA in section 4 and Table 1; this discrepancy does not change assignment, participant counts, or output scoring.

open_questions[4]: The experiment-wide Dreamina versions and Deepseek model version remain unconfirmed despite the illustrated Dreamina version labels (p. 7, Figure 6; p. 8, Figure 7; pp. 5-9, sections 3.3-3.5). Author confirmation or tool-use records would settle actual version exposure. Both tools are explicitly generative AI, so no eligibility criterion depends on this detail.

open_questions[5]: Full contents of the external supplement remain uninspected because both named retrieval routes were network-blocked. Reading the supplement would settle its contents (p. 5, section 3.3; p. 14, Supplementary material). The main text identifies Supplementary Table S1 as the design operation sheet and establishes all eligibility criteria without it.
